chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Barnet band personnel and records 1940-42
summary: Leeman lists Billy May, Bill Miller, Lena Horne, Howard McGhee, Peanuts Holland, Dizzy and Eddie Safranski, and the head arrangements 'Comanche War Dance' and 'Night and Day'.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Then after Al Killian, did you have -- what kind of trumpet players did you have? Leroy? Did he come in then or what?
No.
Al Killian, and who came in after him? Were you there?
No, I didn't work with Al.
Uh huh. Well, you mentioned him with Charlie.
We had, with Charlie Barnet in the years that I worked with him, we had Billy May, and Bill Miller on piano. Billy May was a great arranger.
He still is.
And Lena Horne was with us, and ...
Howard McGee.
A great black trumpet player.
Yeah.
We had Peanuts Holland, a great black trumpet player; Dizzy Gillespie -
Really? Not bad.
Then afterward, we had Eddie Safranski.
Bass -- tremendous bass player. What year was this?
Well, forty --
Between 40 and '43.
Between 40 and '43. Half of '42. Because in the middle of '42 I went with Woody Herman.
Uh huh.
Some of the records we made were a head arrangement -- Comanche War Dance, Night and Day, Leaping at the Lincoln.
Well, that's good -- this is important, this is what we want to know, Cliff.
